source.close_reason: Delivered via PR #96 (merged 3e8ac9c): runtime-owned WAITING_ON_CHANNEL + exact/idempotent SchedulerIntent wake, no agent-facing channel_wait. 10+118 tests pass; tsc clean. Review PARTIAL(expiry intent collision)->repaired(6c0f7d5)->PASS on exact final head.
source.description:
Third comm-runtime bead. When an activation blocks on a pending reply obligation, the RUNTIME transitions it to WAITING_ON_CHANNEL and the scheduler owns resume via SchedulerIntent (exact + idempotent per R2.8) when the correlated reply lands. Agents never poll, never self-mark wakeable, never inspect for arrival.

channel_wait MUST NOT be exposed as the normal agent mechanism — it is at most a diagnostic/escape hatch; semantic waiting is runtime-mediated.

Preserves: single-scheduler invariant (channels.md); scheduler indirection (emitResumeIntent writes intents, never direct enqueue); participant != activation != session identity separation; xtmux owns physical wake/injection mechanics for external runtimes.
source.title: Runtime-owned WAITING_ON_CHANNEL state + SchedulerIntent wake/resume
